headline: US-Iran tensions spike oil above $94, RBA signals rate hike is coming, and OpenAI drops GPT-6 Astra — a big day across markets, geopolitics, and AI.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell last night, dragging down the NASDAQ. Despite strong Azure cloud growth and solid recent earnings, the broader tech sell-off weighed on the stock. Nothing fundamentally broken here — Azure is still growing fast and the long-term AI story remains intact.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google edged lower last night as investors weighed up strong Q2 earnings (revenue up 24%) against ongoing concerns about heavy AI spending. Berkshire Hathaway recently built a stake in Alphabet, which is a vote of confidence in the long-term story.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets dipped today alongside a broader ASX sell-off. Rising oil prices and Middle East tensions add uncertainty to global growth, which tends to weigh on emerging market funds.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped slightly today, largely tracking the ASX 200's 1% fall. With a broad mix of global and Australian shares, it tends to move with the overall market. Nothing to worry about — just market noise.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged down today, reflecting last night's modest S&P 500 dip. US markets were slightly softer across the board but the move is minor.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two eked out a small gain last night. GTA 6 is still on the horizon, though news this week of a UK employment tribunal involving Rockstar (union-busting allegations by fired staff) is a minor distraction. Doesn't change the long-term thesis.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI was flat in today's ASX session. The AI sector globally is in a busy news cycle with GPT-6 Astra launching, but that hasn't moved the ETF today. Sit tight.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS was flat today on the ASX. The lithium story is improving though — spodumene prices are up 121% and Pilbara reported record revenue of $1.93B. The stock hasn't moved yet but the fundamentals are gradually turning more positive.

watch_today.title: RBA flags rate hike may be coming — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: The RBA has issued its bluntest warning yet that it 'may have to raise' interest rates, with multiple major banks now forecasting a November hike. This is a headwind for the ASX broadly and for property-related stocks. If you have a variable rate mortgage, now's a good time to check your budget.

watch_today.title: MSFT — big dip last night, but hold steady
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2% last night, its biggest single-session drop in a while. However, Azure cloud growth remains strong, recent earnings beat expectations, and the AI build-out is ongoing. For a long-term holder, this is a dip in an otherwise solid story — not a reason to sell.

watch_today.title: Oil spikes above $94 — Middle East conflict escalating
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) surged 3% to $94.24 a barrel as US-Iran tensions flared, with exchanges of fire reported and Iran threatening 'economic warfare' and missile strikes. Houthis also attacked Saudi Arabia. Higher oil feeds into inflation, which complicates the RBA's rate decision. Watch this closely.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — flat today but the lithium cycle is turning
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals sat flat today, but the background news is quietly positive: spodumene prices are up 121% and PLS just posted record revenue of $1.93 billion. The stock is still down 27% from your cost base, but the investment thesis — a long-term lithium demand cycle driven by batteries and EVs — is intact. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — flat today, but GPT-6 launch is a tailwind
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF was flat today, but OpenAI just launched GPT-6 Astra, billed as its smartest model yet. A wave of new AI model releases (Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash) is accelerating the sector. Still down from your cost base (-13%), but the long-term AI adoption story is very much alive. Hold.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 dropped 1% today — broad market weakness
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 closed down 90 points (1%) today, dragged by RBA rate hike fears and global uncertainty from Middle East tensions. Your ASX-listed ETFs (VDHG, VGE, VTS) all dipped slightly. This is broad market noise, not a stock-specific problem — no action needed.

world.summary: US-Iran tensions are escalating sharply with military exchanges reported, oil is spiking, and US midterm campaign season is heating up with warning signs for Trump's Republicans.

stories.title: 'Heavy attack': US and Iran exchange fire as Middle East tensions flare
stories.why_it_matters: US and Iranian forces have exchanged fire in what's being described as a 'heavy attack', with Iran simultaneously threatening 'economic warfare' and missile strikes against the US. Yemen's Houthis also attacked Saudi Arabia, adding another flashpoint. This is the most serious escalation in the region in years and has sent oil prices jumping over 3% to $94 a barrel — higher energy costs flow through to petrol prices, groceries, and inflation here in Australia.

stories.title: Iran threatens new 'economic warfare' and missiles as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has explicitly threatened a missile campaign and economic warfare against the US in response to military escalation, while Houthi rebels — backed by Iran — launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia. A wider regional war would disrupt oil shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of the world's oil passes. Markets are nervous, and global inflation could spike if this escalates further.

stories.title: Oil prices surge on Middle East conflict fears and supply risks
stories.why_it_matters: WTI crude oil jumped 3% to $94.24 a barrel overnight — a significant move driven by fears of a protracted war in the Middle East. Supply disruption risks are real given the geography of the conflict. Higher oil prices mean higher fuel costs, which adds to inflation pressure globally and makes central banks (like the RBA) less likely to cut rates.

stories.title: Warning signs abound for Trump's Republicans as midterm campaign enters final sprint
stories.why_it_matters: Reuters reports growing warning signs for Trump's Republican Party as the US midterm election campaign enters its final stretch. Polling and early indicators suggest Democrats may outperform expectations. A shift in Congressional control would affect US fiscal policy, trade decisions, and the broader regulatory environment — all of which flow through to global markets and Australian exporters.

stories.title: As Trump locks in oil deal, Venezuelans ask: What happened to elections?
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has reportedly secured an oil supply deal with Venezuela's Maduro government — a controversial move given the US has long demanded democratic elections in Venezuela. Critics say Trump is trading political values for cheap oil access, while ordinary Venezuelans remain under an authoritarian regime. This has implications for global oil supply and US foreign policy credibility.

markets.summary: The ASX dropped 1% today on RBA rate hike fears and Middle East jitters. Last night, Wall Street was softer but held up relatively well. Oil surged 3% on conflict fears — the standout move of the day.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Dropped 90 points today as RBA rate hike signals and Middle East tensions spooked local investors.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Slipped modestly last night — broad caution but no panic selling.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Slight dip last night, with tech under mild pressure despite solid earnings season.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big move — oil surged 3% as US-Iran military exchanges and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked supply fears.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold nudged higher, acting as a safe haven as Middle East tensions escalated.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was nearly unchanged — a slight tick up, holding around 72 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA has delivered its most direct warning yet that an interest rate rise is coming, social media regulation is dominating the political debate, and millions of workers could be in line for a pay boost.

stories.title: RBA's bluntest warning yet: rates 'may have to rise'
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has issued its strongest language yet on interest rates, saying it 'may have to raise' the cash rate as inflation and business stress persist. Multiple major banks are now forecasting a November rate hike. For anyone with a variable rate mortgage, this is serious — even a 0.25% rise adds hundreds of dollars to annual repayments. The ASX fell 1% today partly on the back of this news.

stories.title: Labor fails to rule out Instagram and TikTok pulling out of Australia
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government is pushing new social media content laws but has refused to rule out the possibility that platforms like Instagram and TikTok could exit Australia rather than comply. One Nation has labelled the laws 'censorship', while critics across the spectrum are questioning whether Labor is trying to tilt political debate by controlling social media feeds. The laws would affect how content is ranked and shown to Australians.

stories.title: Millions of workers tipped for $2,500 pay boost under job-hopping overhaul
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is reportedly planning reforms to job mobility rules that could deliver millions of Australian workers an extra $2,500 a year by making it easier to switch jobs and bargain for higher pay. The proposal targets workplace rules that currently make it harder to take your skills to a competitor for a pay rise. If passed, it would put more money in pockets but could also add to wage-driven inflation — another headache for the RBA.

ai.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra today — its self-proclaimed 'smartest model ever' — though early testers are pushing back. Meanwhile, robots literally marched on a government ministry in Warsaw demanding AI regulation.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, calls it its smartest model yet
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has officially released GPT-6 Astra, marketing it as the most intelligent AI model it has ever built. However, early testers are already pushing back, saying real-world performance doesn't match the hype. It enters a crowded market alongside Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash — with price gaps of up to 13x between the top models. For your GXAI.AX AI ETF, more powerful models mean broader AI adoption, which is a long-term positive.

stories.title: Robots march on Poland's Digital Ministry to demand AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Around 30 robots marched outside Poland's Digital Affairs Ministry in Warsaw, waving flags and chanting slogans demanding stronger AI regulation — organised by a group called 'Democratism'. It's a deliberately theatrical stunt designed to draw attention to what the group says is a dangerous lack of AI guardrails from governments. Whether you find it funny or alarming, it signals that the AI regulation debate is moving from think-tanks to the streets.

stories.title: GPT-6, Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash: Should you switch AI models every time a new one drops?
stories.why_it_matters: With GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash all releasing within weeks of each other, there's now a 13x price gap between the cheapest and most expensive frontier AI models. The rapid pace of releases is causing 'model fatigue' among users and businesses trying to pick a platform. For investors, the key takeaway is that AI infrastructure spending is accelerating — good for cloud providers and AI-focused ETFs like GXAI.AX.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 1 is set — team lists are confirmed, and the Sharks vs Cowboys clash shapes as the blockbuster of the weekend. AFL trade season is heating up with big contract news.

stories.title: NRL 2026 Finals Week 1: All team lists confirmed
stories.why_it_matters: All eight NRL finals teams have locked in their squads for Week 1. The draw features Rabbitohs vs Knights (Friday 7:50pm at Allianz), Warriors vs Dolphins (Saturday 4:05pm in Auckland), Sharks vs Cowboys (Saturday 7:50pm at Allianz), and Panthers vs Roosters (Sunday 4:05pm at CommBank). The Panthers-Roosters clash on Sunday is shaping as the prestige game of the round, with both clubs premiership contenders.

stories.title: Raiders CEO 'quietly confident' of star re-signing ahead of finals
stories.why_it_matters: The Canberra Raiders CEO says the club is 'quietly confident' of re-signing a key star player, though the identity hasn't been officially confirmed. Contract retention during finals season is always a distraction — if the signing gets done, it removes uncertainty heading into the business end of the year.

stories.title: AFL trade news: Geelong midfielder may miss rest of season, Swans face big calls
stories.why_it_matters: AFL whispers suggest a Geelong midfielder could miss the remainder of the season through injury, a significant blow as the Cats push for finals. The Sydney Swans are also facing big selection calls. With AFL finals approaching, injury and team selection news will be critical for clubs battling to go deep into September.

stories.title: Brisbane star speaks on future after major contract decision
stories.why_it_matters: A Brisbane Lions star has spoken publicly about his future following a significant contract development. The Lions are among the AFL's top contenders this year, and uncertainty around key players adds intrigue heading into the finals series. The full details of the contract situation haven't been confirmed publicly, but it's a story to watch as trade period approaches.
